Subject: Initial tenant wiring and compliance gates

Hi Chloe / Ben,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. We're starting the intake for the private deployment and I want to make sure we hand over everything your team needs to stage the tenant in our VPCs. Can you share a concise checklist of the mandatory items we should prepare on our side (networking, keys, accounts, evidence for SOC2 checks, routing, egress controls, etc.)?

Specifics we'd like to cover up-front:
- Required CIDR(s) / VPC sizing guidance and whether Redwood needs a peered VPC or an interconnect
- Which ports/protocols must be allowed for health checks and control plane traffic
- KMS/HSM expectations: customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed, and any certificate formats you need
- Audit logs / retention windows we should enable (and any file formats for evidence)
- Expected public egress IPs or NAT recommendations for external callback endpoints
- Any procurement/legal artifact you want ahead of the kickoff (DPA, certificate lists)

Also please point me to a template for the network wiring and a list of the people we should include for a short technical kickoff. We can run an internal scan before the meeting to avoid surprises.

We plan to start the technical kickoff next week — earliest availability is Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,

Hi Raj — thanks, this is perfect. Below is a compact, action-oriented intake checklist we use for private (VPC / on-prem) tenants. I've attached the wiring template and our SOC2 evidence request PDF for your security team.

Redwood private-deploy intake checklist (high level) — items for Acme to provide before technical kickoff:
1) Account & contact basics
   - List of technical contacts (name, email, phone, role) + escalation contacts
   - HubSpot account ID / PO number (if procurement is already in motion)
2) Network & connectivity
   - Primary VPC CIDR and any additional CIDRs (suggest non-overlapping /24 blocks for tenant workloads)
   - NAT/Egress approach: confirm whether you want a single egress IP per region or per-subnet NAT
   - Required public endpoints we must reach (if any) — include FQDNs and ports
   - If using cloud interconnect: peering details or VPN termination point + ASN and BGP expectations
3) Firewall / security group rules
   - Allowlist for control plane health checks (list included in wiring template)
   - Minimum required inbound ports: 443 (control plane), 10250 (agent), ephemeral as noted in template
4) Identity & keys
   - KMS: do you want customer-managed keys (CMK) in your KMS, or do you prefer Redwood-managed keys? If CMK, provide KMS key ARN and owner IAM role we can assume for encrypt/decrypt tests
   - Service account / IAM role we will use for provisioning with scoped permissions (we provide a least-privilege role template)
5) Audit & compliance evidence
   - Retention windows required for logs (default we recommend 90 days for onboarding evidence)
   - Provide any SOC2 / HITRUST-specific artifacts upfront if you want them validated before go-live
6) Routing & DNS
   - IP prefixes we should route to (and any blackhole prefixes)
   - DNS delegations or ns records if we need to create private records in your zone
7) Operational readiness
   - Backups / snapshot window and RTO/RPO targets for tenant data (if applicable)
   - Monitoring endpoints and expected SLAs (we provide a monitoring hook for your team)

Optional but useful: a simple network diagram (your internal diagram is great) and sample terraform/CloudFormation snippets for the peering side.

Attachments:
- redwood-vpc-wiring-template.xlsx
- soc2-evidence-request.pdf

Next steps / proposed kickoff participants:
- Acme: Raj Patel (Infra), Sarah Lim (Security), network owner (CIDR authority)
- Redwood: Chloe Martin (SRE Solutions), Ben Carter (Private Deploy PM), Kimberly Park (Network Eng)

We can run a short pre-kickoff technical readout (30 minutes) to validate CIDRs and KMS choices before the full kickoff. Tue/Wed morning PT works for us.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127

Thanks Raj / Chloe — quick operational notes to add to the checklist:
- For predictable egress behavior we recommend a NAT gateway per AZ if you expect heavy outbound model-callback traffic; otherwise a centralized NAT with SNAT mapping is fine for small volumes.
- Health checks originate from a small set of IP ranges (listed in the wiring template). Please confirm those are allowed so our probes don't get blocked.
- KMS: if you provide a CMK we'll run a small encrypt/decrypt smoke test during provisioning; please add the Redwood provisioning role to the key policy with sts:AssumeRole capability.
